accuracy.evidence: Definitions checked against NC Year 3 Geometry (identify horizontal and vertical lines and pairs of perpendicular and parallel lines), CCSS 4.G.1 and the NCETM Year 3 geometry guidance: parallel = same direction and constant distance, never meeting; perpendicular = meeting at a right angle; horizontal/vertical judged against the ground. Grid checks verified by cross and dot products: from (2,6), (4,5) is parallel to A's (4,−2) and (1,4) is perpendicular. Letter kinds checked in a sans-serif font: T perpendicular only, Z and N parallel only, H both, V neither.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented slips (Ryan and Williams; NCETM): parallel must be equal length or horizontal, 'not touching on the page' taken as parallel, perpendicular must be one flat and one upright line, horizontal/vertical treated as fixed regardless of orientation, and swapping the two words. Each is a prediction option, a look-alike pair, or a tagged challenge answer.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagparperp turns line B against a fixed line A with live gap bars at both ends and dashed extensions that mark where tilted lines meet, a 2×2 look-alike pair picker, a square-corner finder on a slanted line, a letter-stroke classifier and a dot-grid draw that copies or turns A's steps. flagangle names and sizes single angles and flagsym folds shapes; neither compares a pair of lines. Shingle gate passed.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner sees the gap numbers differ and the red 'they meet here' dot before reaching parallel, so 'never meet' is discovered from the same-gap bars; the perpendicular step only goes green at a square corner between two slanted lines; the grid step turns the idea into a drawing rule (copy steps vs turn steps) that the practice items reuse.

predictions.evidence: Six predictions with tempting wrong options: 'still vertical' for a turned flagpole, 'yes, because they do not touch', 'no, they are not the same length', 'no, one line must be flat and one upright', 'perpendicular lines' for Z, and 'draw it flat, because parallel lines are flat'. The lab disproves each.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions; wrong answers are tagged swap, hv, touch, length, upright or vee and each message names the slip: words swapped, describing one line instead of a pair, not touching ≠ parallel, length irrelevant, tilted perpendiculars, V's strokes meet.

readability.evidence: Kid text Flesch-Kincaid grade 2.9 (family target ≤ 5) with an everyday example in each paragraph (table top, flagpole, rails, book corner); adult text 6.5 (≤ 10) after splitting the mistakes and lab paragraphs into short sentences.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passed: no filler phrases, under 12% overlap with any lesson (including 103 parallel and perpendicular slopes, which is about gradients). Kid paragraphs: horizontal/vertical, parallel, perpendicular, the not-touching trap. Adult: placement, meaning, mistakes, what the lab does.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 screenshots of all seven steps in both themes: the 'hanging string' label was clipped at the right edge on the first pass, so it moved inside and split onto two lines; the letter feedback was split onto two lines; grid rows were pulled up so the status line no longer touches the bottom dots; pair cards end above the message line. Turn buttons are 4 across and wrap cleanly.

accessibility.evidence: Every drag has buttons: ↺/↻ 5° and 15° turn buttons with descriptive aria-labels, Pair 1–4 buttons with aria-pressed, four letter-kind buttons, and ←→↑↓ buttons that move B's end one dot. The canvas aria-label states the result after each move (e.g. 'B is perpendicular to A'). walk.cjs axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
